2016_102_122016mtg.paragraph: Troy School District's Board of Education met in regular session at 7:00 PM on December 20, 2016 at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan, taking up the October 2016 Treasurer's Report, a 2016-17 General Fund budget amendment, bond construction Bid Pack #18, a roofing bid, and adoption of a rewritten Board policy book. The amendment sets the General Fund appropriation at $144,758,462 against budgeted revenues of $144,948,253 and a budgeted ending fund balance of $21,722,076 at June 30, 2017. The evening was also the final meeting for retiring trustees Ida Edmunds and Wendy Underwood.

**Meeting.** Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, December 20, 2016, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools. Agenda: recognition, consent agenda, 8.A Budget Amendment (packet p. 122), 8.B Bond - Construction Bid Pack #18 (p. 129), 8.C Roofing Bid (p. 134), 10.A Approve Board Policy Book (p. 138).

**Recognition.** Final meeting for two retiring trustees: Wendy Underwood, more than 11 years of service, and Ida Edmunds, more than 31 years.

**Consent agenda.** November 1, 2016 workshop minutes (6:02 p.m. to 9:48 p.m.; Kevin Sutton of Lusk Albertson, Jim Crowley and Paul Stauder of the PFM Group), November 15, 2016 meeting minutes, and the October 2016 Treasurer's Report. The November 15 minutes carry Motion 16-087 (consent agenda), Motion 16-088 (bond resolution) and Motion 16-089 (Mr. Hauff to the NSBA Advocacy Institute, Washington, D.C., January 29-31, 2017), each Yes 6 / No 0 with Mr. Schmidt absent. The bond resolution authorizes 2017 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) not to exceed $40,000,000, the second series under the November 5, 2013 election authorization of not more than $125,000,000; the first series, the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds of $52,710,000, was issued January 29, 2014. Maturity is not later than sixteen years at a true interest cost not exceeding 5.00%, with Stifel, Nicolaus & Company as underwriter, Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone as bond counsel and Public Financial Management, Inc. as financial advisor.

**Item 8.A - Budget Amendment.** General Fund appropriation of $144,758,462; revenues amended from $143,026,065 to $144,948,253; beginning fund balance July 1, 2016 restated at $21,532,285; excess revenues from 77,660 to 189,791; budgeted ending fund balance June 30, 2017 $21,722,076. **Item 8.B - Bid Pack 18** (RFP 9829, issued October 28, 2016). Award total $3,362,380.00, of which $2,992,853.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and $369,527.00 from the Food Service budget: Blue Start demolition $14,100.00; Hewett Company exterior doors $537,505.00; Paint Plus $35,217.00; Stafford Smith food service equipment $100,063.00; CSM mechanical $873,173.00; Contrast mechanical $418,000.00; MCMI controls $392,150.00; Great Lakes Power electrical $686,500.00; contingency $305,672.00.

**Item 10.A - Board Policy Book.** Bylaws and policies rewritten over four months with Kevin Sutton of Lusk Albertson PLC and first read at the December 6, 2016 workshop. The manual sets Board compensation at $100.00 per annum, a $5,000 fixed-asset threshold, a minimum year-end general fund balance of fifteen (15) percent, and budgeting in conformity with GASB 54.

Troy School District's Board of Education convened its regular meeting at 7:00 PM on December 20, 2016 in the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098 (district office 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000); meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at vimeo.com/troyschools. Business items were 8.A Budget Amendment (packet p. 122), 8.B Bond - Construction Bid Pack #18 (p. 129), 8.C Roofing Bid (p. 134) and 10.A Approve Board Policy Book (p. 138).

RECOGNITION. December 20, 2016 was the final meeting for two retiring trustees: Wendy Underwood, leaving after more than 11 years of service, and Ida Edmunds, retiring after more than 31 years.

CONSENT AGENDA. Item 5 comprised the November 1, 2016 workshop minutes, the November 15, 2016 meeting minutes and the October 2016 Treasurer's Report. The November 1 workshop at the Administration Building ran 6:02 p.m. to 9:48 p.m. under President Philippart with all seven members present, Superintendent Machesky, Kevin Sutton of Lusk Albertson, and Jim Crowley and Paul Stauder of the PFM Group; topics were Series 2 - 2014 School Building & Site Bonds, a stormwater management resolution, review of policies Sections F, G, H & I, and a book study of Blindspot.

NOVEMBER 15, 2016 MINUTES. Called to order at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building with Mr. Schmidt absent and roughly 50 members of the audience; adjourned 7:41 p.m. Wrestling coach Don Hill, who started coaching at Troy High in 1967 and is celebrating his 90th birthday, was recognized in connection with the National Wrestling Hall of Fame. Motion 16-087 approved consent items including the September 2016 Treasurer's Reports (Yes 6, No 0, Schmidt absent). Motion 16-088 (Yes 6, No 0) adopted a resolution authorizing bonds designated 2017 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation) in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed Forty Million Dollars ($40,000,000), the second series under the special school election of November 5, 2013 at which electors approved not to exceed $125,000,000; the first series, the 2014 School Building and Site Bonds in the original principal amount of $52,710,000, was issued January 29, 2014. Terms: denominations of $5,000 or integral multiples; final maturity not later than sixteen (16) years from issue; negotiated sale at a true interest cost not exceeding five percent (5.00%) per annum; book-entry through The Depository Trust Company and Cede & Co. The resolution appoints Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated as senior managing underwriter and placement agent, Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. as bond counsel and Public Financial Management, Inc. as financial advisor; cites Act 451 of 1976, Act 34 of 2001 and Act 92 of 2005; and requires an unlimited tax levy commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2017. Motion 16-089 (Yes 6, No 0) approved Mr. Hauff's attendance at the NSBA Advocacy Institute Conference in Washington, D.C., January 29-31, 2017. Superintendent Machesky reported Team Schroeder's recognition as a National Blue Ribbon School, with Kris Griffor, Principal Brian Canfield and teachers Lindsay Keegan and Karen Bush receiving the award, and a $10,000 grant from ATT and the Troy Community Foundation.

ITEM 8.B - BOND CONSTRUCTION, BID PACK 18. RFP 9829, issued October 28, 2016, covered mechanical and electrical upgrades at Barnard, Bemis and Wass Elementary Schools and the Administration Building, door replacement at Troy and Athens High Schools, gravity relief hoods at Boulan and Larson Middle Schools, and a kitchen renovation at International Academy East; bids were reviewed by TMP Associates, Peter Basso & Associates and Barton Malow. Rob Carson, Director of Maintenance & Operations (1140 Rankin, Troy, MI 48083), transmitted the recommendation to Rick West on December 15, 2016. Awards: Blue Start demolition $14,100.00; Hewett Company exterior doors $537,505.00; Paint Plus painting/floors $35,217.00; Stafford Smith food service equipment $100,063.00; CSM mechanical (Barnard, Bemis, Wass, IAE) $873,173.00; Contrast mechanical (Admin, Boulan, Larson) $418,000.00; MCMI temperature controls $392,150.00; Great Lakes Power electrical $686,500.00; contingency $305,672.00; total $3,362,380.00, with an apparent low bidder total of $3,056,708.00. Funding: $2,992,853.00 from the 2014 Capital Projects Fund and $369,527.00 from the Food Service budget. The BP 18 budget summary totals $4,809,692.00, including Bemis $1,201,241.00, Wass $1,055,033.00, Barnard $969,058.00, Admin $665,057.00 and Athens doors $404,320.00.

Public Bid 9830, the 2017 Troy School District Roof Program, was issued November 9, 2016 for roof replacement at Barnard and Wattles Elementary Schools, International Academy East, and Athens and Troy High Schools, plus restoration at Morse Elementary. WeatherTech Consulting Group, Inc. (Geof Garabedian and Ann Crippen; 7747 Auburn Road, Utica, MI 48317) reported a mandatory pre-bid conference on 11/21/16 with seven bidders and six sealed bids read aloud on 12/01/16. Awards: J.D. Candler (printed J. D. Chandler in the resolution) $300,300.00, comprising Barnard $293,800.00 and Morse restoration $6,500.00; Royal West $873,316.00; 10% contingency $117,362.00; total $1,290,978.00. The Carson memorandum states the total roofing work to be completed in 2017 as $1,173,616.00, with Morse restoration commencing spring 2017 and replacements June through August 2017, funded from the Capital Projects Fund and Operational Fund.

ITEM 10.A - BOARD POLICY BOOK. Over four months, Board members and administration worked with Kevin Sutton of Lusk Albertson to update the Bylaws and Policies; a first reading was held at the December 6, 2016 Board Workshop. The manual, copyrighted to Lusk Albertson PLC, runs 0000 Introduction through 8000 General Policies. Governance: seven members on six-year terms elected at the November general election in even-numbered years; officers elected annually in January for one-year terms; the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services appointed Treasurer annually as a nonvoting officer; compensation of $100.00 per annum. Chapter 5000 Business requires a budget adopted prior to July 1 each year, prepared in conformity with GASB 54, an endeavor to maintain a minimum year-end general fund balance of fifteen (15) percent, monthly financial reports, an annual independent audit presented at a public meeting, credit-card payment no later than 60 days from the initial statement date, and a fixed-asset threshold of $5,000. Other provisions include two epinephrine auto-injectors per building and transportation eligibility at one mile for elementary students and one and one-half miles otherwise.
